Feb 16, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Amir Houieh shared positive travel experiences to Munich, noting welcoming people and securing accommodation via an affordable Airbnb, while Noémi Biró updated the group on wedding planning, including a vendor awaiting a permit and establishing current pricing with a quote for services like catering and tent rentals. Gabor Kerekes introduced a new hardware/software project called "Nexus," conceived as an anti-distraction "meta OS" for deep thinking, which Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes agreed should radically rethink technology's model, and Gabor Kerekes confirmed developing a local transcription pipeline for Nexus. Participants, including Noémi Biró, reviewed the scope for the next phase of development, which focuses on building an open beta for two specific modules, R&D on memory and proactivity, and ensuring safety and App Store readiness with an iOS wrapper, while Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh discussed long-term involvement, hiring a third engineer, and moving the R&D website online.
Details
Travel Experience and Accommodation in Munich: Amir Houieh recounted that many people traveled by train to Munich, noting the overall experience was positive. They discussed accommodation, which was secured via an affordable, clean Airbnb located about an hour's drive from Munich (00:02:51). A humorous anecdote was shared about accidentally navigating to a completely different city due to a bug when using an iPhone link on an Android device after the demo (00:04:05).
Perception of Munich and German Cliches: Amir Houieh shared positive impressions of Munich, noting that the people were welcoming and accommodating, actively trying to help even when they could not speak English. They mentioned that the negative cliches about Germans not wanting to speak German, which they frequently observe in Dusseldorf, were not evident in Munich (00:04:05). The shared effort among attendees at an event, described as "a quarter of a million" strong, was noted as a powerful experience (00:05:21).
Update on Wedding Planning and Vendor Communication: Noémi Biró updated the group on their wedding planning, mentioning an administrative weekend focused on house matters. They explained that after having a call with the wedding planner on Friday about a vendor's lack of response, the planner intervened and reported that the vendor was awaiting a permit, which while not new information, provided a sense of relief due to outside involvement (00:05:21). They also received a quote from the planner for services such as catering and tent rentals, helping to establish an understanding of current prices (00:06:50).
Discussion on Wedding Venue and Delegation: The group discussed the possibility of the wedding planners setting up an event in a non-traditional location, such as a field, requiring them to build the entire infrastructure. Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh agreed that even with full delegation to a planner, there would still be significant work involved, emphasizing that delegating tasks is beneficial and saves "brain cells" (00:08:04). Gabor Kerekes shared that the aim for the wedding is a "laidback" and "lowkey" celebration that feels like a sophisticated garden party or barbecue, even if it cannot be entirely "perfect" (00:09:05).
New Project Obsession: Anti-Distraction Hardware and Software: Noémi Biró introduced a new obsession of Gabor Kerekes with e-ink hacking and hardware development for specialized devices. Gabor Kerekes was inspired by a device developed for people with ADHD and deep thinking, which led to the discussion of creating a specialized system, tentatively code-named "untangle" or "Nexus" (00:11:47) (00:15:13). This device uses an LCD screen that emulates the feel of e-ink but with a fast refresh rate, making it intentionally anti-addictive and anti-distracting (00:13:30).
Strategy for Developing and Partnering for "Nexus": Gabor Kerekes expressed a desire to develop a prototype of "untangle" (now "Nexus") and potentially collaborate with the creators of the inspiration device, asking for a development unit to continue prototyping (00:15:13). They clarified that "Nexus" is envisioned as a "meta OS" or an "ADHD OS," rather than an application, which could potentially be combined with the idea of a browser-based OS. It was noted that the target audience for "Nexus" aligns with those who value attention and use anti-distraction devices (00:19:09).
Rethinking the Model: From Treatment to OS Redesign: Amir Houieh suggested a more radical approach for "Nexus," questioning the fundamental model of technology like the existence of apps, rather than just treating current problems (00:21:47). Gabor Kerekes agreed, suggesting that the "medium is the message," and that a device with a slow display and lack of features like video consumption inherently conditions attention towards deep thought. They noted that using a stylus and handwriting to interact with AI could create a very different, less distracting user experience (00:23:08).
Updates on Project Work and Agreement Outline Review: Amir Houieh confirmed they finished the "carefinder project" and are now available for other work, having started on the "Nexus" project (00:24:32). They drafted a contract agreement outline, and Gabor Kerekes suggested specifying the two modules in more detail to prevent scope creep, while acknowledging the four-month timeline (00:25:46). The two main drivers for the next phase were identified as the modules for "six weeks after pregnancy loss" and "trying to conceive again" (00:29:02).
Scope of Work for the Next Phase of Development: The goal for the next phase is defined as building an open beta and maintaining high development velocity through an iterative process (00:29:02). The scope includes core research and development (R&D) on memory and proactivity, and the development of new modules, such as guided programs, which will include features like journaling (00:30:24). Noémi Biró clarified that journaling should be viewed as a tool within a broader program module, not a separate module itself, suggesting a reframing of the agreement language (00:33:01).
Safety, Infrastructure, and Exclusions in the Agreement: The scope of work also includes UI/UX evolution (like improving articles display), safety and guardrail implementation, and creating a learning infrastructure with an analytical dashboard for the client (00:34:35). The plan includes monthly consultations with clinical advisors and developing an iOS wrapper (which enables push notifications) to facilitate App Store availability, instead of a full native iOS app (00:35:49). Items excluded from the scope were B2B/clinic readiness, local small language models, and infrastructure migration, though they agreed to budget for infra work to harden security and prepare for potential future handover (00:37:09).
Long-Term Involvement and Hiring Strategy: Gabor Kerekes expressed being less convinced about long-term involvement in the current project, but they agreed to maintain open communication about future collaboration after the four-month period (00:42:35). They discussed returning to the R&D lab model and the need to hire a third engineer or assist the client in finding a CTO. Gabor Kerekes identified a potential US-based, full-stack design engineer who is aligned with the project's values, though they noted the cost implications and the need to work within the current budget (00:45:40).
Analytics and Feedback Organization: Gabor Kerekes confirmed that session length analytics, showing time spent talking, can be derived from conversations without breaching security protocols like Google Analytics, and they will follow up on this to send out last week's data (00:48:19). They have been organizing feedback into a structured document and plan to read a document about the distress tier framework for the project (00:49:31).
R&D Website and Article Preparation: For the R&D website, the team confirmed they are moving forward with cherry-picking blog posts to include (00:49:31). Gabor Kerekes requested the latest article be moved to a Notion page to facilitate easier comment submission for review (00:51:38).
Focus Areas for the Current Week: Amir Houieh's focus for the week includes advancing the "Nexus" project by creating one or two use cases, possibly by integrating local data or testing with a therapy app. A key objective is to get the R&D website online and announce the company's new focus on social media to redirect inquiries from investors who may be interested in the R&D direction (00:53:04). They discussed maintaining relations with design-oriented investors, such as those from Designer Fund, who understand the vision for generative UI and dissolving the concept of apps (00:54:55).
Discussion of Website Gradient and Visuals: Gabor Kerekes detailed an exploration into generating gradients and visual shaders for the website, initially stemming from the sub-optimal appearance of colors when optimizing loading (00:59:15). Gabor Kerekes showed interest in using strong visuals to catch attention, potentially using a platform to generate no-code shaders, but determined this visual experimentation required more work and should be wrapped up for now, suggesting they would return to it later (01:01:50). Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes agreed that the current subtle visual presets were sufficient for the present and that the visual elements should evolve over time (01:05:09).
Upcoming Work and Time Off: Amir Houieh asked Gabor Kerekes about their plans for the week, learning that Gabor Kerekes plans to go to the countryside to celebrate their birthday and have some unstructured time. Gabor Kerekes intends to take their laptop but is aiming for a period of creative space and unstructured thinking, rather than production-focused work (01:07:36). Amir Houieh suggested that before leaving, Gabor Kerekes should connect the Nexus project with the idea of walking and recording, exploring potential applications (01:08:51).
Implementation of Local Transcription Pipeline: Gabor Kerekes confirmed that they had already coded a local transcription pipeline using Whisper to transcribe conversations on the machine (01:08:51). The pipeline can take a directory of audio files, produce transcripts with speaker identification (diarization), and create text files that can be fed into the Nexus project. The participants agreed to formally name the project "Nexus," and Amir Houieh will begin renaming it across all files (01:09:52).
Next Steps for Nexus and Analytics: For immediate work, Gabor Kerekes needs to handle website changes related to a "cu thing" and then focus on the Nexus implementation, integrating it with the audio app. Amir Houieh will be focusing on the civil analytics and then plans to add persistent storage to Nexus using SQLite, which they identified as the easiest and lightest method for maintaining state in an application. The participants agreed to meet again at three (01:11:05).
Suggested next steps
Noémi Biró will rewrite the part of the agreement about the modules for clarity, specifying that the amount is to be defined as they go.
Gabor Kerekes will follow up with Amir Houieh after the meeting to get the analytics for the time spent in the app from last week.
Gabor Kerekes will read Kira's document to understand the implications of patterns for cibil and make a copy of the latest article to provide comments on notion.
Amir Houieh will talk to a bookkeeper to determine if they need to continue using body as a company or if they can work freelance with the CBIL contract.
Gabor Kerekes will push his changes to the website today and then work on the Nexus implementation integration with the audio app.
Amir Houieh will add a persistent storage using SQL light to Nexus.
Amir Houieh will start renaming the project to Nexus everywhere.
Amir Houieh will focus on the analytics from a civil perspective.
